content.value_statement: APIs often expose sensitive data through weak authentication, poor validation, and missing abuse controls. This skill guides secure design for REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket services.
actual_capabilities: Explains JWT authentication and refresh token handling.
Shows authorization checks for protected API routes.
Demonstrates input validation with parameterized queries and Zod.
Covers rate limiting, Redis-backed quotas, and DDoS controls.
Provides API security checklists aligned with OWASP API Top 10.
limitations: Provides guidance and examples, not an automated vulnerability scanner.
Requires adaptation for each framework, data model, and deployment environment.
Does not replace penetration testing, threat modeling, or expert security review.
Example code must be reviewed before production use.

use_cases.title: Design Secure Endpoints
use_cases.description: Plan authentication, authorization, validation, and error handling before building new API routes.

use_cases.title: Review Existing APIs
use_cases.description: Check services for weak tokens, missing authorization, injection risks, and missing rate limits.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Create repeatable API security checklists for engineering teams and release reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single API route.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API endpoint for authentication, authorization, validation, error handling, and rate limiting. Explain the highest risks first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Secure Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a safer login and token flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a secure authentication flow for this API. Include token lifetime, refresh token handling, secret storage, and abuse prevention.

prompt_templates.title: Harden API Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these request fields and database operations. Recommend validation rules, safe query patterns, and output sanitization steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Release Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release-ready API security checklist for this service. Cover OWASP API risks, monitoring, rate limits, CORS, headers, and data protection.

output_examples.input: Review a login endpoint for security gaps.
output_examples.output: The response identifies token handling, brute force protection, generic errors, and password storage as the main review areas.

output_examples.input: Plan defenses for a public reporting API.
output_examples.output: The response recommends authentication boundaries, per-user quotas, Redis-backed rate limits, safe validation, and monitoring for unusual usage.

output_examples.input: Prepare an API security checklist for launch.
output_examples.output: The response groups checks by authentication, authorization, input validation, rate limiting, data protection, logging, and OWASP API coverage.

best_practices: Adapt every example to your framework and verify it with tests.
Use environment-managed secrets and rotate them when access changes.
Review authorization for each object and action, not only each route.
anti_patterns: Copying example code into production without threat modeling or tests.
Relying on JWT authentication while skipping resource-level authorization.
Returning raw errors or stack traces from API endpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill scan APIs automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and review prompts for human-led API security work.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is listed as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What API styles does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers REST, GraphQL, and WebSocket security concepts at a guidance level.

faq.question: Does it replace a security audit?
faq.answer: No. Use it to prepare and improve code before formal review or penetration testing.

faq.question: Why does it include vulnerable examples?
faq.answer: The examples show unsafe patterns so users can compare them with safer alternatives.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide endpoint behavior, authentication requirements, data sensitivity, expected traffic, and relevant framework details.
